title: The Gloria (Luke 2:14)
hookLine: the angels' song from Bethlehem, silent in Advent and Lent
carry: glory to god in the highest

cards: Go back eighty days, to the shepherds. A night on the hills outside Bethlehem: sheep, cold, a fire, nothing happening. Then an angel, a light, terror, and the news: a child is born.
And suddenly, Luke says, there's a whole crowd of angels, a heavenly army, praising God. It's the first Christmas song, and it's one line long.

Every Sunday, right after asking for mercy, the church picks up that song and keeps going. For four weeks before Christmas and six weeks before Easter, it goes quiet. And when it comes back, the bells ring.

teach.b: Here's the angels' line, in the Douay-Rheims: "Glory to God in the highest; and on earth peace to men of good will." In Latin, Gloria in excelsis Deo.
That's where the hymn starts, but the Gloria at Mass goes much further.

Christians in the first few centuries kept singing after that line, adding praise upon praise. In Latin: laudamus te, benedicimus te, adoramus te, glorificamus te. Praise, blessing, adoring, glorifying.
Then it turns to Jesus as the Lamb of God, who takes away the world's sins, and asks his mercy. It ends with the Father, Son and Holy Spirit, like the Glory Be you learned, but bigger.

That's why it's sometimes called the greater doxology: the Glory Be is the little glory-word, and this is the big one. Notice where it sits. Right after the church asks for mercy, it bursts into praise.
Sorry, then glory. And it isn't sung every week. In Advent, the weeks before Christmas, it's left out, so the angels' song can come back new on Christmas night.
On Holy Thursday, it's sung while every bell in the church rings, and then the bells go silent until Easter.

teach.h: GLORY TO GOD IN THE HIGHEST.
teach.b: At the Easter Vigil, the Gloria returns, and the bells ring again. One small scholar's note: the King James Bible reads good will toward men. The Latin tradition reads peace to men of good will.
The difference is one letter in some Greek manuscripts.

how: The Gloria is sung or said after the Kyrie at Sunday Masses outside Advent and Lent, and on solemnities and feasts; on Holy Thursday and at the Easter Vigil the church bells ring during it.

games.q: it's the first Sunday of Advent. Mass reaches the place right after the Kyrie where the Gloria usually goes. what happens?

games.why: it's left out for the four weeks of Advent, so the angels' song comes back new on Christmas night.

practice: If you pray, say or hum one line: glory to God in the highest. Quietly is fine, tunelessly is fine; the shepherds weren't choir material either.
If you don't pray, find one thing that's simply good, something that asks for nothing back, say so out loud, that's beautiful, and sit with it.

wordCard.voice: Gloria. The angels' song from Bethlehem, grown into a hymn of praise at Mass, and kept silent in Advent and Lent. Today's word.
